The curtain, rebuilt so it cannot be cut in the wrong pixels - after the second look at a live client (a tablet on The Forge), where 1.2.16 still drew one black column and the GM lost the sidebar tabs.

- **The curtain lives in the body, not inside `#interface`.** A fixed element inside a zoomed or transformed interface is sized and clipped in that ancestor's pixels; the glass came out as a column because its frame was wider than the screen. The curtain is now a child of the body, right before `#interface`, its box is the viewport, and its position, size and layer are written inline from glass.mjs, so no stylesheet order can move it. Its z-index is read from `#interface` so it always paints just under the interface and above the board.
- **Nothing is forced on Foundry's columns any more.** The rule that put `position: relative; z-index: 1` on `#ui-left/#ui-top/#ui-middle/#ui-right/#ui-bottom` is gone; the interface stacks above the glass by itself now.
- **The GM's sidebar keeps its height.** The shift that puts the tabs below the corner pane is capped at 160 px and applied as padding (border-box), so the sidebar shrinks instead of running off the bottom of the screen.
- **The tiles' shard is cut for the real tiles.** The port left the design page's mock selectors in the tile measurement, so the shard under the scene controls and the sidebar tabs was cut for a fallback box; it now measures `#scene-controls` and `#sidebar-tabs`.
- **The tile styling matches Foundry's buttons** (`button.ui-control`) and beats the base sheet's own `!important`s.
- **A watchdog** rebuilds the curtain at 4 and 9 seconds after ready if it is unpainted or its box is not the viewport.
- **Diagnostics in the Settings window:** the Look fieldset shows one line about the curtain (frame, box, layer, panes, self-check, blocks) and a "Redraw the glass" button. If the glass still looks wrong, that line is what to send. `drpgGlassDebug()` in the console prints the full picture.
